text:
Stock was flat today, up just 0.7%, after a sharp two-week decline that saw it drop from $424 to $392. The modest bounce comes as refining margins remain supported by tight crude supply — US crude at $107 per barrel — but uncertainty about oil direction is weighing heavily on the sector. Wall Street openly admitted on September 22 it doesn't know where oil prices are headed, particularly given tensions around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, which keeps traders cautious about refiners' near-term outlook.

The stock's weakness over the past few days reflects confusion in the broader energy market rather than company-specific problems. Diesel storage remains tight at 107.9 million barrels, and refineries are running hot at 96.8% capacity, which normally supports refiner profits — but talk of a potential US diesel export ban, plus conflicting signals on Iran negotiations and the Ukraine situation, has left investors unsure whether oil prices will trend higher or settle down. Without clarity on geopolitics or policy, refiners face difficult betting conditions.
